gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-thaana: Tightly packed letters with a single-weight stroke give Bevellier its cut-paper look. Noto Sans Thaana lets wide channels lead into each counter, so the crowded heading above gets room to breathe.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-yi: Noto Sans Yi has a deep midsection in its lowercase and rounds left open like an unlatched hook. And Bevellier hums along above it, soft and featureless, in a single weight.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-zanabazar-: Noto Sans Zanabazar Square stands tall with a soaring x-height and wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp. Bevellier leaves a rolling-ball-pen trail up top; the body keeps small text legible.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-traditional-nus: Noto Traditional Nushu moves like a broad-nibbed pen that never curls shut. Its bowls fill the line, while Bevellier above holds to one monoline stroke and tightly fitted letters.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-orienta: Orienta has counters that breathe like a hollow reed cut open, with capitals barely taller than lowercase. But Bevellier above it keeps every stroke free of brush-style pressure swell and its letters tightly fitted.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-oxygen: Thread-stitched strokes, packed tight: that is Bevellier at its best. Oxygen does the quieter job best, its curves never closing back on themselves and its lowercase nearly matching the capitals.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-pathway-extreme: Bevellier's strokes are as plain as stitched thread outlines. Pathway Extreme would read steadily line after line, its rounded letters open and its short ascenders sitting under a towering x-height.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-radio-canada-big: Bevellier packs its high, wide-looking letters close together, each stroke cut at a single weight. Radio Canada Big then fills the line with a tall x-height and monoline strokes whose terminals finish away from the stem.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-ruda: Bevellier sets the tone with tight, single-weight letters. Ruda brings a sizable x-height, a wire-like monoline skeleton and wide-mouthed rounds, so reading on and on feels light and unhurried.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-saira: Bevellier draws wirelike strokes of one thickness, packed tightly into a high, wide-looking lowercase. Saira keeps a see-through gap in each s and lets its rounded letters stretch toward the top line.
